top_problem: The tabla is not actually a shared-row grid: the name bands, subheads and item rows of side-by-side cards sit 72 pt (row 1) and 36 pt (row 2) apart because the shorter list is padded with an inflated face, so across the gutter nothing lines up and El Barril/La Botella read as half poster, half list; the boldest missing idea is a true lotería tabla where every card shares one face height and one band line, with the lists (not the pictures) absorbing the difference, so the whole page reads as one printed game board.
fixes: Lock all four name bands to one face height per row (e.g. 105 pt) so the bands sit at 210 pt and 582 pt on both cards, and let subheads and item rows share the same baselines across the gutter.

Absorb the list-length difference below the lists instead of in the figure (move La Botella and El Barril extras into the list: add the spirit descriptions and a card-foot verse or cut-paper rule) so no card has a 141 pt barrel dwarfing four beers.
Use one description measure on every card (La Rosa is 183 pt versus 205 pt elsewhere) so descriptions break to the same right edge in both columns.
Give the three spirits their own description lines so La Botella's item pitch matches the 12 pt name + 12 pt description rhythm of the other cards instead of a tighter, different cadence.
Align the verse column to one x across all four cards (currently 90/162/90/126 pt) so the face template is one fixed grid, not four scaled variants.

measurements.header_level_ambiguity: the masthead 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' (h 10.32) is tagged as the same 'header' level as the card names, so there are two styles at one level in the data

top_problem: The card-name bands, which carry the menu's category hierarchy, sit at different heights across each row (25.4 mm apart in row 1, 12.7 mm in row 2), so the section headers and subheads do not align across columns and the eye zig-zags. The boldest missing idea: make the name band the shared horizon of each row, so all four lotería 'titles' read as one set strip like a real tabla, with the figures growing above it and not pushing it down.
fixes: Lock the El Cantarito and El Barril name bands to the same y (and the same for La Rosa and La Botella) by absorbing height differences below the lists or in the face above a fixed band line, so the first subheads in each row share one baseline.

Raise the subheads (CLÁSICOS, DE BARRIL, etc.) to at least 8.5-9 pt with heavier weight or the card colour, so the level 2 heading clearly outranks the 11 pt item names and does not read as a caption.

Promote the English category gloss in each band ('Cocktails', 'Beer & Cider', 'Wine', 'Spirits · straight pours') from small italic to a legible secondary line; 'Spirits · straight pours' is overloaded, so trim it to 'Spirits'.

Set a single fixed space above every non-first subhead measured from the previous baseline (for example 12 pt), including after items that have no description such as Añejo Tequila above COÑAC, which currently sits visibly tighter.
Give the masthead its own 'title' level in layout.elements and in the type scale, so card names are the only 'header' level and the hierarchy is title > card band > subhead > item.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling

measurements.price_style: Fraunces 700 11.5 pt tnum+lnum in the card colour on all 4 cards; item names 10.5 pt; card numerals 11 pt italic ink

contrast.note: marigold is used only for frames, band fill and pennants, never for text

top_problem: The lotería concept is real, but colour does no narrative work past the card frames. Prices are just tinted numerals in four hues, one of them a muddy substitute ochre, and the 11 pt italic card numbers read as stray footnotes rather than the lotería's signature big corner numerals. The boldest missing idea: make the Don Clemente numbers and the prices one confident numeral system (large lotería-style corner numbers, prices in the same lining face on a shared tint chip), so the numbers become the menu's graphic voice.
fixes: Replace the brown #8A5A00 La Botella prices with ink or a deepened marigold (around #9A6400 or darker, still at least 4.5:1) that clearly belongs to the marigold family, so the palette stays four hues plus neutrals instead of adding a fifth muddy one.
Put the same pour label style on every wine price: add 'copa' (or 'botella' if it is a bottle price) to Brut Rose's 13 so the La Rosa price column uses one format.

Enlarge the lotería card numbers to 20-24 pt Fraunces in the card colour, top-left as on real Don Clemente cards, so they read as a deliberate numeral motif rather than an 11 pt italic that looks almost like a price.

Balance face tints against the card body: the La Rosa pink face and the El Barril grey-green face are much quieter than the El Cantarito and La Botella faces, so give all four faces one tint strength (about 12-15% of the card hue).

Fill the empty lower-left of the El Barril face and the lower right of the La Botella list, for example by moving the verse under the figure or adding a thin price-rule ornament, so no card shows dead cream space next to a dense neighbour.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country

top_problem: The lotería idea shows up as trim but never becomes the menu's structure. Four framed cards under a papel-picado garland is the go-to 'Mexican menu' look. To fill the grid, the figures now range from 69 to 141 pt, so El Barril and La Botella are half illustration and half thin list. The tabla stops reading as one deck of equal cards. The venue also has no name or mark: the title is the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar'. The boldest missing idea is a full tabla: every card on the same face template at the same figure scale, with the drinks list set as the card body, and a house-owned masthead in place of the stock papel picado banner.
fixes: Put every card face on one fixed height and one figure scale, as on a real lotería deck, and absorb the row difference by setting a spirit or beer feature, or bottle/pour columns, in the short card's list rather than by inflating the barrel and the bottle to 141 and 105 pt.

Swap the generic papel-picado garland and 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' title for an ownable masthead: the venue's name drawn as a lotería-style header card, or a tabla frame around the whole deck, so the top of the page carries the concept instead of stock festive trim.

Raise the card numbers from 11 pt italic in the corner to the confident corner numerals of real lotería cards, in a boxed or bold style that is clearly not a price, so the lotería idea reads at arm's length.

Give the beer, wine and spirits lists the same richness as the cocktails with a second spec line (style/ABV, grape/region, agave/age in a muted italic), so the bottom row and El Barril stop reading as thin filler under large illustrations.

Tighten the name bands so the Spanish name and the English gloss sit on one fixed left inset per band instead of floating centred groups of different widths, which makes the four bands match the column grid below them.

lens: phone version and print/phone coherence (preview-phone.png vs preview-letter.png)
top_problem: The phone stack is actually the better-proportioned version: every card has a compact face and the list leads. On print the 2 x 2 grid forces the El Barril and La Botella faces to fill 49% and 55% of their cards, which inflates the figures and leaves cream voids. As a result the two formats feel like different menus. The missing bold idea is to make the lotería tabla work as the ordering system itself (a card to point at or call out, cantor-style, on both paper and phone), not just a frame around four lists.
fixes: Give print and phone the same face proportions: cap the face at roughly 30% of every card on print (as on phone), and use the space you gain for the drinks list or a shared footer, instead of scaling up the barrel and bottle to fill a 177 pt / 141 pt face.

Label the phone chip tabs with the card names ('44 Cantarito', '9 Barril', '41 Rosa', '8 Botella'), and give every tab a visible active and inactive state, because bare numerals mean nothing to a guest as navigation.

Use one name-band text colour: La Botella's dark ink on marigold breaks the cream-on-colour rule of the other three bands in both formats, so darken the band (or use an ochre band) and keep the text cream.

Make the phone papel picado repeat the print sequence and colour rhythm (terracotta, marigold, agave, rosa), and bring the gloss and verse type sizes into the same ratio to the item names in both formats, so the two read as one system.

Rebalance the thin cards on both formats (Barril, Rosa, Botella) with a consistent footer device per card, such as a card-number seal or cantor line, so the short lists do not end abruptly under large faces.

lens: Every item and price vs build/draft_doc.json, descriptions and ingredients, section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: All 14 draft items and prices match exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Old Fashioned 16, Daiquiri 14, Pilsner 7, IPA 8, Amber 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rose 13, Blanco 12, Anejo 16, Cognac VSOP 18). Nothing is invented, and the cocktail glass and garnish cues trace to recipe_versions in doc.meta.designer_notes. The problem is the agave card. In a Mexican cantina it is the last and smallest card, and its three spirits print as bare name-plus-price lines: the round deleted the draft's own descriptions ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'Anejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.') and printed no type or age wording. Beer has no ABV and wine has no grape or region line either. So only the cocktails meet criterion 8, and the four categories are not treated equally.
fixes: Give each La Botella spirit a one-line description built from known facts (for example 'Unaged blanco tequila, served neat.' / 'Aged anejo tequila, served neat.' / 'VSOP-grade Cognac, served neat.'), or restore the draft's descriptions, and print a small 'ask your server' flag for the missing brand, age and pour size instead of leaving the lines blank.

Beer and cider: keep the draft descriptions but print the style words the data supports (Pilsner / IPA / Amber Lager / Cider) consistently, and keep ABV visibly flagged as pending, so every beer line follows one pattern instead of reading as a placeholder.

Wine: name the grape in each description from known facts ('Malbec, dry red.', 'Pinot Grigio, dry white.') and flag region and producer as pending; resolve whether Brut Rose is priced by the glass or the bottle, because it is the only wine price with no label.

Make doc.json's section order match the printed tabla (Cocktails, Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits); doc.json currently runs Cocktails, Spirits, Beer, Cider, Wine, so the phone and HTML order can drift from the print order.
Give agave weight that fits the venue: move La Botella up (swap it with La Rosa), or add an agave cue to its gloss, so tequila is not the least-described category on a Mexican cantina menu.

lens: ingredient names and description completeness (draft: build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: Description completeness falls apart after the cocktails. The spirits card (Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP) prints names only with no description at all, which fails the scorecard check that every item has a description element. Beer and wine get generic one-liners ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') with no ABV, region or producer. Everything missing is correctly flagged in missing_ingredients, and nothing is invented. All 14 items and prices match the draft exactly, the 2x2 reading order (cocktails, beer and cider, wine, spirits) is correct, and the cocktails name the spirit, modifiers and garnish.
fixes: Give each spirit a short factual description line built only from sourced category facts (for example 'Unaged 100% agave tequila' for Blanco only if a gateway row supports it, otherwise the category name), so no item prints name-only, and keep brand, age and pour flagged.

Get ABV and brewery for the three draft beers and the cider, and ABV and region for the three wines, through the Coordinator's needs_input, then print them in one consistent position (for example 'Czech-style pilsner · 4.8%' and 'Mendoza, Argentina'); until the answers arrive, replace the thin one-liners with the draft's own style words and leave nothing implied.

Resolve Brut Rosé's missing serve label so the wine card's price column is consistent: either confirm 'copa' or 'botella' and print it like Malbec and Pinot Grigio, or drop the 'copa' labels card-wide.

Print a dairy/allergen marker on the Brown Butter Old Fashioned once the venue confirms it (flagged as 'allergen confirmation' in missing_ingredients); a butter-washed spirit with no guest-facing note is a content risk.

Give the La Botella spirits card the same description-and-serve rhythm as El Cantarito (description line plus italic serve cue) so the four cards read as one system instead of a detailed cocktail card next to a bare price list.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The order follows the generic bar sequence (cocktails, beer, wine, spirits), not a cantina's. Agave, the venue's signature and highest-margin pour, sits last in the weakest bottom-right spot on the smallest card with no descriptions. Beer, the lowest-margin category, holds the prime top-right slot, and its illustration fills 49% of that card for four one-line items. The 2 x 2 grid also has no clear reading path: the name bands are offset by 72 pt and 36 pt within each row, so the eye cannot tell whether to read across or down.
fixes: Swap La Botella and El Barril so agave sits top-right next to El Cantarito (cocktails, then agave, then wine, then beer and cider), and give the tequila card the prime row. Coa Cantina (ref 572) leads with agave for this reason.
Shrink El Barril's 177 pt illustration panel and give the space to content or a reading cue. The low-margin beer card should not hold more illustration than the cocktail card.

Fix the reading order inside the tabla by aligning the name bands in each row, or by numbering or ordering the cards so print and phone read in the same sequence. Confirm the phone tabs use the same order as print.

Make the pour labels consistent: 'copa' appears on Malbec and Pinot Grigio but Brut Rosé's price has no label. Either hold Brut Rosé under a clearly marked pending label or apply one labelling rule to every wine price (needs_input 5).

Send the missing facts (beer ABV and style detail, wine grape and region beyond 'Dry red wine', tequila brand, age and pour size) through needs_input 2, 4 and 6 before print. Until they arrive, the beer, wine and spirit cards are much thinner than the cocktail card and the menu reads unevenly.
problems: Section order is the generic sequence rather than one built for a cantina: agave is last and has the least prominent position.
The prime top-right spot goes to four low-margin beers under a 177 pt barrel illustration (49% of the card).
Name bands within a row do not align (72 pt and 36 pt offsets), so the 2 x 2 reading path is unclear.
Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP have no descriptions. They are flagged in missing_ingredients but print bare.
Beer descriptions give no ABV and wine descriptions give no region ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). Both are flagged, not invented, but fall short of criterion 8.
Brut Rosé's price has no glass or bottle label, while the other two wines are labelled 'copa'.
There is no non-alcoholic section and no mezcal or Mexican lager. These were correctly asked about (needs_input 7), not added.
All 14 prices match the draft exactly: nothing invented, changed or dropped. Junmai Ginjo is correctly left off and flagged.

top_problem: The menu reads in two voices. The cocktails get full, appetising copy with a serve cue, but the other three cards drop to flat, database-style one-liners: 'Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.', 'Dry sparkling cider.'. The spirits print with no description at all, because the draft's 'Blanco tequila pour.' / 'Añejo tequila pour.' / 'VSOP Cognac pour.' were removed and nothing replaced them. So the drinks categories are not treated equally, and the bilingual lotería concept stops at the card faces while every line of item copy stays plain English. All 14 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly (nothing invented, changed or dropped). The missing ABV, region, producer and pour data is properly flagged in needs_input 2-6.
fixes: Write every non-cocktail description to the same template and length as the cocktails, using only draft facts (for example Malbec: 'Dry red; by the copa.'; Dry-Hopped IPA: 'Hop-forward IPA on draft.'), and hold a visible slot for the ABV, region and pour data asked in needs_input 2-6 so the four cards read as one voice.

Put back a one-line sourced description under Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP (the draft's own 'pour' lines, rewritten in the menu's voice) so La Botella is not the only card with bare names; add the pour size to the band gloss once the venue answers.

Make the subhead glosses one pattern of true translations: 'TEQUILA · Agave' and 'COÑAC · Brandy' break the SPANISH · English rule, and the band gloss 'Spirits · straight pours' is the only two-part gloss (use 'Spirits' in the band, like 'Cocktails' / 'Wine')..

Keep the copy consistent and inside the draft: 'fresh lime' adds a claim the draft does not make (it says 'lime'). Also align 'house demerara syrup' (Daiquiri) with 'demerara syrup' (Old Fashioned), or source the 'house' distinction.

Replace the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' title with the venue's name (needs_input 8). Resolve needs_input 10 by swapping the two drunkenness-joke verses (El Barril, La Botella) for non-drinking verses, so the menu's tone agrees with responsible service and with the warmth of the other two cards.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged (draft: build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: Missing data is flagged honestly in proposal.md: all 14 draft items are present, all 14 prices match, nothing was invented, and needs_input items 1-12 cover the gaps. On the printed page, though, those gaps become empty or filler copy. The 3 spirits have no description line at all (no type, age or brand), so La Botella reads as a price list. The beer copy has no ABV, and the wine copy has no region. Lines like 'Dry red wine.' and 'Crisp pale lager.' only restate the category. Brut Rosé prints an unlabelled price next to two wines labelled 'copa'. Manhattan prints 'aromatic bitters' even though the draft hides it (public_components aromatic-bitters:false). The designer chose that override and flagged it, but the draft snapshot has not been approved to change.
fixes: Until the venue answers flag 11, follow the draft's public_components and drop 'aromatic bitters' from the printed Manhattan line (the draft hides it), leaving it in the proposal as a flagged question.

Give each spirit a known-fact line from beverage_categories and the draft (for example 'Blanco / plata, 100% agave class per NOM' only if sourced, otherwise just 'Blanco' / 'Añejo' / 'VSOP' as the class) so no item prints with a name alone; keep brand, age and pour size in missing_ingredients.

Resolve the Brut Rosé label (flag 5) before approval. Until then, pick one printed treatment for all three wines: either label every wine price, or move 'copa' up into the 'Por Copa' subhead so no price is ambiguously labelled.

Put a clear hold on this proposal so it cannot print until the venue sends beer ABV, wine region and spirit age: add a machine-readable blocking list in doc.meta.missing_ingredients keyed by item id, so the gaps can't slip through as filler copy like 'Dry white wine.'.

For a Mexican cantina, raise the agave card's weight. At the moment, La Botella is the last and emptiest card, and the cantina gaps (Mexican lager, mezcal, agua fresca, flag 7) leave the flow cocktail-heavy. Keep asking for those items rather than adding any.

lens: I traced every printed ingredient, garnish, glass, serve and subhead label on round 15 back to its source. Sources were the draft_doc.json components and the gateway log_id 191 join from phg.menu_items to phg.recipe_versions on current_recipe_version_id. Every serve cue and garnish matches. Margarita, rv f06abb74: glassware Rocks, garnish Lime wheel, method 'strain over fresh ice', printed as 'On the rocks, lime wheel.' Manhattan, rv 9fb77eaa: Coupe, Cocktail cherry, printed as 'In a coupe, cocktail cherry.' Brown Butter Old Fashioned, rv 7095fd3d: Rocks, Orange peel, method 'over a large cube', printed as 'Over a large cube, orange peel.' House Daiquiri, rv 14d45e57: Coupe, Lime coin, printed as 'In a coupe, lime coin.' The ingredient words also trace to draft components: Fresh Lime Juice, Agave Syrup (prep), Demerara Syrup (prep, 'House 1:1'), Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Aromatic Bitters. Every beer, cider and wine description is the menu_items.menu_description word for word, and all 15 prices match menu_price. Four printed facts do not trace to a source. First, 'aromatic bitters' on the Manhattan prints against the draft's meta.public_components {aromatic-bitters:false}. Second, the Spanish subhead 'COÑAC' (the source row and item name spell it 'Cognac'). Third, 'TEQUILA' as the Spanish half of 'Agave': it is not a translation, so the SPANISH · English pattern breaks. Fourth, 'copa', which carries no pour size.
top_problem: The facts are clean, but the copy is not. Six of the 13 lines are taxonomy-grade stubs ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.', 'Toasty amber lager.', 'Dry sparkling cider.', 'Hop-forward draft IPA.'), and the three spirits print as name and price only, with no brand, age or pour. For a cantina, the menu also has one agave cocktail, no Mexican lager, no mezcal and no agua fresca, and two of the four verses joke about drunkenness. It reads as a generic bar list dressed in lotería trim, not as an Iowa City cantina.
fixes: Replace the six stub descriptions with guest-language copy once the venue answers needs_input 2-4 (brewery, ABV, producer, region), and flag them missing_ingredients until then instead of printing class labels like 'Dry red wine.'

Make every subhead a true SPANISH · English pair: change 'TEQUILA · Agave' to 'AGAVE · Agave' or 'TEQUILA · Tequila', and change 'COÑAC · Brandy' to 'BRANDY · Brandy' so the Spanish word does not clash with 'Cognac VSOP' printed directly below it.

Label the Brut Rosé price ('copa' or 'botella') and add the pour size to the 'copa' labels and the spirits (for example '1.5 oz') once the venue supplies them; right now one wine price is ambiguous next to two labelled ones.

Resolve the Manhattan bitters conflict before print. menu_items bf732e78 menu_description includes 'aromatic bitters', but the draft's public_components hides it; get the venue's answer to needs_input 11 rather than overriding silently.

Designer note (layout, not my edit): swap the El Barril and La Botella drunkenness verses (needs_input 10) for non-drinking lotería verses, and fill El Barril's oversized empty face; with only one cocktail item it signals the agave-led cantina emphasis weakly, so ask the venue for a mezcal or a Mexican lager (needs_input 7).

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: There is no single guest voice. The four card verses are lively and Mexican, but eight of the thirteen items carry flat catalogue copy that repeats the item name or its category: 'Dry red wine.' / 'Dry white wine.' (Malbec, Pinot Grigio), 'Toasty amber lager.' (Amber Lager), 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' (Dry-Hopped IPA), 'Dry sparkling cider.' (Dry Cider), 'Dry sparkling rosé.' (Brut Rosé), plus Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP with no description at all. Among the cocktails, only the Margarita gets a flavour lead ('Bright and citrus-forward'); the other three are bare ingredient lists. Facts check out: the gateway query (log_id 190) against phg.recipe_versions confirms Margarita f06abb74 Rocks / Lime wheel, Manhattan 9fb77eaa Coupe / Cocktail cherry, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d Rocks / Orange peel / 'strain over a large cube', House Daiquiri 14d45e57 Coupe / Lime coin, and every beer/wine/cider line matches phg.menu_items.menu_description word for word. The problem is the voice, not the accuracy.
problems: Criterion 12, at the automatic-fail line: Amber Lager 'Toasty amber lager.', Dry-Hopped IPA 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', Dry Cider 'Dry sparkling cider.' and Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé.' mostly repeat the item name. Malbec 'Dry red wine.' and Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine.' are category labels, not guest language (source: phg.menu_items.menu_description, printed word for word).

Criterion 12: the three spirits (Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP) print name and price only. The draft lines 'Blanco tequila pour.' / 'Añejo tequila pour.' / 'VSOP Cognac pour.' were rightly dropped, but nothing replaces them, so this card reads like a price list.

Criterion 12, uneven cocktail voice: Margarita opens with a flavour line ('Bright and citrus-forward:'), while Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned and House Daiquiri are comma lists. Within one card, two registers sit side by side.

Criteria 10 and 13: the Spanish dichos (including two drinking jokes, 'La herramienta del borracho.' and 'Tanto bebió el albañil...') are the strongest voice on the page, and the English item copy under them is utilitarian. The menu reads as a festive wrapper around a generic bar list. It also has no mezcal, no Mexican lager and no agua fresca/N.A., which an Iowa City cantina guest would expect (the proposal asks about this in needs_input 7; nothing was invented).

Criterion 14: Brut Rosé has no pour label while Malbec and Pinot Grigio say 'copa' (the draft price label is empty, so this is correctly flagged but still unlabelled). La Botella items have no second line, so that card's rhythm differs from the other three.

Criterion 11, minor: 'fresh lime' / 'house demerara syrup' come from draft_doc components 'Fresh Lime Juice' and the prep note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup' (both acceptable). The Manhattan prints 'aromatic bitters' against draft meta.public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false}. This is disclosed (needs_input 11) but it is an unresolved visibility override.
fixes: Rewrite the Margarita, Manhattan, Old Fashioned and Daiquiri in one pattern (a short sensory lead from sourced words, then the ingredients) so the four cocktails share one register. For the Manhattan and Old Fashioned, use method rows 9fb77eaa 'Stir with ice and strain' and 7095fd3d 'strain over a large cube' (e.g. 'Stirred and silky:' / 'Stirred, over a large cube:').

Ask the venue for one guest-facing flavour or origin fact per beer, wine and cider (brewery, region, tasting note). Until then, stop printing the name-echo lines as if they were descriptions. Set them as a quiet style tag (e.g. 'Pale lager · draft') so they don't look like failed copy.

Give the spirits card a sourced line under each item from beverage_categories (04d72e1f 'Blanco / plata', 9f4dae69 'Añejo', a88f6e79 'Cognac', bec5063c 'VSOP') in guest wording, e.g. 'Blanco / plata, unaged' only if a row states it. Otherwise add a one-line card note inviting the guest to ask for today's pours.
Bring the English copy closer to the dichos' warmth, or tone the dichos down (resolve needs_input 10 on the two drinking jokes), so the page reads in one voice.
Label the Brut Rosé pour (copa or botella) once the venue confirms it, so all three wine prices carry the same label.

lens: Venue-type fit: Mexican cantina and cocktail bar, Spanish and lotería usage including verses, census ZCTA 52240 (gateway log_id 192)
top_problem: The lotería wrapper is authentic, but the drinks inside do not read as a cantina. All four verses match the traditional Don Clemente cards word for word: El Cantarito 44 'Tanto va el cántaro al agua, que se quiebra y te moja las enaguas', El Barril 9 'Tanto bebió el albañil, que quedó como barril', La Rosa 41 'Rosita, Rosaura, ven que te quiero ahora', La Botella 8 'La herramienta del borracho'. The Spanish subheads are correct (CLÁSICOS, DE LA CASA, DE BARRIL, SIDRA, POR COPA, ESPUMOSO, COÑAC). But of 13 items only the Margarita is an agave cocktail. The card is called El Cantarito, yet it sells no Cantarito and leads into a Manhattan and a Daiquiri. The beer card opens with a Czech Pilsner and has no Mexican lager. ZCTA 52240 is a college district: median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, median household income $52,960, 11.0% Hispanic/Latino.
